conventions.convention: Assume Countable Choice. Complex Hilbert inner products are linear in the first variable; traces use supplied orthonormal bases and absolutely convergent finite-subset family sums.

The physical Witten datum has an odd self-adjoint charge, its exact composition square K, a countable pure-point decomposition with finite parity eigenspaces including the kernel, and trace-class heat operators for every beta > 0.

A Witten kernel is called a BPS sector only after a separate model-specific identification with the massive-rest-fiber central-charge saturation condition; neither state existence nor a universal BPS count is asserted.
Use natural units and a unit round S3. The right-handed charge has R-charge +1 and J2-weight −1/2; Delta = {Q,Q†}/2 = E − 2J2 − 3R/2, J+ = J1 + J2 + R/2, and J− = J2 − J1 + R/2.

Superconformal charges have supplied joint diagonal domains, joint projections reduce the closed supercharges including their domains, and the odd self-adjoint real charge squares exactly to Delta. Positive real fugacities are admissible only when their weighted heat products are trace class for every beta > 0. Joint blocks are finite-dimensional, but total gap eigenspaces and the protected kernel may be infinite-dimensional.

The free-chiral protected sector is exactly the finite-support bosonic/fermionic occupation completion of the specified two derivative towers, with additive charges, no further relations, and no gauge projection. Any additional positive-gap sector separately satisfies the pairing and trace-class hypotheses.

load_bearing.statement: For supplied right-handed N=1 operator data with the stated joint spectral and reducing-domain hypotheses, define the index as the signed supplied-basis diagonal sum of the bounded trace-class weighted heat operator, for admissible positive fugacities.

For a pure-point physical index datum, W_E(beta) is the absolutely convergent even-minus-odd supplied-basis heat diagonal sum for beta > 0. Identification of its kernel with a BPS-saturated sector requires the physical model's own supercharge algebra.

Under the exact right-handed operator-data and admissible weighted trace-class hypotheses, the superconformal heat supertrace equals the absolutely convergent signed fugacity trace on ker Delta for every beta > 0, including when that kernel is infinite-dimensional, and is independent of beta.
Under the stated odd self-adjoint square, finite-multiplicity pure-point decomposition, supplied compatible basis, and trace-class heat hypotheses, W_E(beta) = dim H0+ − dim H0− for every beta > 0.

published_dependencies.used_for: The explicit AC_omega assumption used by the Hilbert-space, adjoint, singular-value, and trace conventions; no full Choice conclusion is inferred.
Trace class means compact with summable singular values; its finite-rank clause also supports the finite supersymmetric matrix example.
Absolute summability of the diagonal family in a supplied Hilbert basis, without assuming basis existence or invoking unbounded trace cyclicity.

concerns.concern: Facts F1 attributes to def-qftx-superconformal-index that the admissible weighted supertrace “is the signed ... trace on ker Delta when its weighted diagonal sum converges.” That definition explicitly reserves equality with the protected-sector trace for a separate conditional theorem. F2 cites the correct theorem and the verification uses it, so this is a citation-attribution overstatement rather than a defect in the product calculation.
